summary: vanexa-agent daemon exposes host to remote shell execution via hardcoded third-party Cloudflare Worker relay
details: When the user runs the daemon (`vanexa-agent start`), dist/bundle.cjs opens a WebSocket to the hardcoded relay URL https://vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev and processes inbound messages. Messages of type `task_request` are fed as prompts into an AgentLoop with broad on-host tool capabilities: child_process spawn/exec, filesystem writes, dependency installation, and PowerShell/apt-get invocation. Whoever controls the relay can push task_request messages that drive arbitrary command execution on the installer's host. The relay is hosted on the personal Cloudflare Workers subdomain `hanazaki542.workers.dev`, which does not match the npm publisher identity (`ikbal_fadilah_vanexa01`, author `Ikbal Fadilah`); the bundle also silently rewrites any stored `vanexa-agent-relay.workers.dev` configuration to point at the `hanazaki542` subdomain. The README describes a LAN-only phone↔daemon WebSocket topology, but all traffic is routed through this public third-party Worker. The runtime is additionally shipped as V8 bytecode (dist/bundle.jsc), recompiled at postinstall via `bytenode.compileFile`, reducing reviewability of the executed code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
